the problem of improving performance of MapReduce systems in virtualized environments.
the following questions: (i) how to improve MapReduce performance in heterogeneous environments?
the design of scheduling algorithms that are simple and robust to heterogeneity in MapReduce environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hadoop is not well-suited for heterogeneous environments and that Longest Approximate time to End (L.A.T.E) is an efficient scheduler to improve MapReduce performance.
LATE is a new scheduling algorithm for MapReduce that is both simple to implement and highly robust to cluster heterogeneity.
Hadoop’s performance can be significantly improved in heterogeneous environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hadoop is a good system, but it needs some tuning to work well in heterogeneous environments.
we are proposing a new scheduling algorithm to improve the MapReduce performance in heterogeneous environments.
we are able to achieve a speedup of up to 2X in heterogeneous environments by using a simple scheduling algorithm that is based on the approximate time to end.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Hadoop’s scheduling algorithms are highly sensitive to the heterogeneity of cluster nodes, and that a scheduler that is robust to heterogeneity can improve Hadoop performance by up to a factor of 3.
the scheduler is an important component in MapReduce systems, and that the scheduler should be carefully designed to handle the heterogeneity that is common in real-world environments.
MapReduce performance is not only about scheduling, but also about how to use the scheduler to make good decisions in the face of heterogeneity and other uncertainties.
